content: A tuberculin skin test involves the intradermal injection of 1 mL of purified protein derivative (PPD), equivalent to 5 tuberculin units. The test result is evaluated 48 to 72 hours after administration. A positive result is indicated by an induration greater than 10 mm. For patients with heightened sensitivity, 1 tuberculin unit may be used, while 250 tuberculin units may be administered if there is no response to the standard 5 tuberculin units. Adverse events following the administration of any vaccine, including this test, can be reported to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) at 1-800-822-7967. Potential adverse reactions include rash, itching, vesiculation, ulceration, necrosis, pain, and hypersensitivity. Individuals with a history of a positive tuberculin skin test may exhibit suppressed responsiveness within six weeks of a viral infection or inactive tuberculosis. The tuberculin test contains soluble growth products derived from the tubercle bacillus. Old tuberculin (OT) is a culture filtrate of uniform potency, but PPD is a more refined and preferred product. Multiple puncture devices (e.g., Aplitest, SclavoTest-PPD, Tine Test-PPD) are less sensitive than intradermal administration. Several factors can reduce the ability to respond to the tuberculin test, including infections (e.g., viral infections like measles, mumps, chickenpox, HIV), live virus vaccinations (e.g., measles, mumps, rubella), bacterial infections (e.g., typhoid fever, brucellosis, typhus, leprosy, pertussis, overwhelming tuberculosis, tuberculous pleurisy), fungal infections (e.g., South American blastomycosis), certain medications (e.g., corticosteroids, immunosuppressive agents), metabolic disorders (e.g., chronic renal failure), low protein states (e.g., severe protein depletion, afibrinogenemia), age (e.g., newborns, elderly individuals with waning sensitivity), stress (e.g., surgery, burns, mental illness, graft-versus-host reactions), diseases affecting lymphoid organs (e.g., Hodgkin’s disease, lymphoma, chronic leukemia, sarcoidosis), and malignancy. Any condition impairing cell-mediated immunity, including aging, can result in a false-negative reaction. Test reliability decreases in HIV-infected individuals as CD4 counts decline. Tuberculin should not be injected subcutaneously. If this occurs, no local reaction develops, but highly sensitive individuals may experience a general febrile reaction or acute inflammation around old tuberculous lesions. The predictive value of the tuberculin skin test depends on the prevalence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and the relative prevalence of cross-reactions with nontuberculous mycobacteria. To prevent the transmission of infectious agents, a separate, sterile, single-use disposable syringe and needle must be used for each patient. Before administering Aplisol, the patient’s history should be reviewed for any immediate-type hypersensitivity to the product, prior use of the agent, or contraindications to the test. Epinephrine should be readily available in case of an anaphylactoid or acute hypersensitivity reaction. Improper storage or handling of the drug may result in a loss of potency and inaccurate test results. Reactivity to the test may be suppressed for up to 5–6 weeks following immunization with certain live viral vaccines, viral infections, or discontinuation of corticosteroids or immunosuppressive agents. The safety of this test during lactation is unknown, as it is not clear whether the product is excreted in breast milk. During pregnancy, the test is classified as Category C, meaning that while no controlled studies in pregnant women have shown evidence of fetal risk, caution is advised. The antigenic purified protein derivative (PPD) of Mycobacterium tuberculosis sensitizes patients to specific antigenic components of the organism. The onset of action for the test is approximately 5–6 hours, with peak effects observed at 48–72 hours. This information is provided for general educational purposes. For the most current and specific details, consult the applicable healthcare provider or plan.
